title: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner
hook: the Fashioner, who shapes every face differently (59:24)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Khaliq: the Creator who measures, plans and brings into being. Your line was made.

A train station at rush hour: faces, faces, faces. Two eyes, a nose, a mouth, every single time. The same few parts, and no two alike. Add everyone alive now and everyone who lived before, and each face is still its own. How many ways can two eyes and a mouth be arranged? Apparently, enough. Right after the Creator, the same verse in al-Hashr names the one who gives each thing its shape. Today: Al-Musawwir, the Fashioner.
screen: `A TRAIN STATION FULL OF FACES.` → `THE SAME FEW PARTS.` → `NO TWO ALIKE.`

segments.voice: Pickthall calls al-Musawwir the Fashioner. The root is s-w-r, with the heavy s, sad, and it gives surah: form, shape, image, a different word from the surah of the Qur'an. Tasawwur, imagining, forming a picture in the mind, comes from the same root. So al-Musawwir gives every created thing its particular form: this face, this leaf, this fingerprint. In Al 'Imran, He is the one who shapes you in the wombs however He wills. In at-Taghabun: He shaped you, and made your shapes good. In al-Infitar, from the juz' just read: He created you, then fashioned you, then proportioned you, and in whatever form He willed, He put you together. In ar-Rum, the differences in people's languages and colors are called among His signs. Not a problem to be fixed. A sign. Because the word for image is from this root, Muslim scholars have long discussed making pictures of living beings. Some, drawing on hadith, discouraged it; others permit some kinds, like photographs. Mosque walls in that tradition carry calligraphy, geometry and vines rather than faces. Then a hadith turns the whole name around. Muslim records the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saying: Allah does not look at your forms, your suwar, or your wealth. He looks at your hearts and your deeds. The Fashioner made every face, and then chose not to judge by it. That leaves a question for anyone who looks at faces.
screen: `S-W-R — FORM, SHAPE, IMAGE.` · `SHAPED IN THE WOMB, SHAPES MADE GOOD.` · `COLORS AND LANGUAGES AS SIGNS.` · `HE LOOKS AT HEARTS, NOT FORMS.` · then, large: `EVERY FACE SHAPED.`

segments.voice: Hold up one hand and look closely: the lines across the palm, the creases at each knuckle, the whorls at your fingertips, a pattern nobody else has. Bring to mind a face you love and find one detail you've never really looked at, a laugh line, an eyebrow, the way the mouth rests. Give the same slow look to a face you passed today and barely saw, then to your own: one of a kind, never made before and never again.
Al-Musawwir. The Fashioner, who gives every created thing its own form, and every face its own shape. Today's word.
Your line: every face shaped. Even the ones passed without a look. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims reflect on the variety of human faces, colors and languages as signs of the Fashioner; mosque art, shaped by scholarly discussion of image-making, tends to use calligraphy, geometry and plant forms rather than figures.

original.note: Arabic: the Fashioner, who gives each thing its form; from s-w-r, image, shape.

trapdoor: what you thought: God as an artist.
what it means: the one who gives every created thing its own form, and then judges hearts, not faces.
what a scholar hears: s-w-r gives sura and tasawwur; 3:6, 64:3, 82:7–8; Muslim 2564, not your suwar but your hearts; the image-making debate.
